title: Gold Rebounds Above $4,100 Despite Strong US Payrolls, Ahead of Inflation Test
excerpt: Spot gold traded at $4,121.77 on Monday after Friday's 165,000-job payrolls surprise knocked it toward $4,033 — Tuesday's US CPI print now decides whether the rebound holds, with December hike odds near 80%.
body:
• Gold reclaimed $4,100 on Monday, trading at $4,121.77, after reversing Friday's losses, FXStreet reported; TradingKey put the intraday high at $4,134.27.
  • Friday's US Nonfarm Payrolls rose 165,000 in October, well above the 65,000 expected, and unemployment fell to 4.1% — a print that pushed December Fed hike odds to about 80% on the CME FedWatch Tool.
  • Even after Friday's dip toward $4,033, gold gained about 5% on the week, its largest weekly advance since late August, TradingKey reported.
  • What decides the next move: US CPI on Tuesday, November 10 — a hot print could seal a December hike and revive selling; resistance sits at $4,191-$4,201, support near $4,070.

Gold is back above $4,100 at the start of a decisive week, reversing the losses it took on Friday after a far stronger than expected US jobs report. Spot gold traded at $4,121.77 on Monday, FXStreet reported, and rose more than 1% intraday in Asian trading to touch $4,134.27, according to TradingKey.

What the jobs report did — and why gold recovered

US Nonfarm Payrolls increased by 165,000 in October, blowing past expectations for a 65,000 gain, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2% in September, the Bureau of Labor Statistics figures cited by both reports show. The dollar and Treasury yields jumped on the print, and the odds of a December Federal Reserve rate hike rose to about 80%, where they now waver, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool cited by FXStreet. Gold fell toward $4,033 on Friday before settling near $4,065.

Monday's recovery had different drivers. The dollar retreated as reduced US-Iran geopolitical tensions dragged oil prices lower and eased inflation concerns — President Donald Trump said on Sunday he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress — and renewed US-China trade optimism weighed on the dollar, FXStreet reported. China's Finance Ministry said on Monday it will extend the suspension of an additional 24% tariff on imports from the United States for two months, effective November 10. Separately, gold demand in India picked up at the start of a key festival on Friday as prices slid to a seven-month low, drawing back bargain hunters, Reuters reported via FXStreet.

The CPI test

Traders remain sceptical ahead of Tuesday's US Consumer Price Index release. A surprise uptick in underlying inflation could seal in a December rate hike and revive bearish sentiment around gold, because higher rates raise the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset, FXStreet noted. On the charts, FXStreet put initial resistance at the 50-day moving average of $4,191.19 and the 100-day at $4,201.38, with immediate support at the 21-day average near $4,069.59 — a daily close below that level would likely open a deeper pullback. For now, the week's arithmetic is simple: gold absorbed a payrolls print nearly three times forecast and still closed the week about 5% higher, its largest weekly advance since late August, TradingKey reported. Whether buyers can defend $4,100 through the inflation print is the question Tuesday answers.
